spans.dates: the week of March 6 to 10 will be International Affairs week on the Wesleyan campus
spans.opening: The week's festivities will begin with a speech by Bishop G. Bromley Oxnam in Monday's chapel.
spans.midweek: Next Wednesday, Donald Smith, Chief Deputy of Personnel of Foreign Service will speak in Chapel.
spans.closing: A panel discussion by various foreign students from this campus will officially close International Affairs Week on Friday.

spans.count: Eight of the original 13 OWU Woodrow Wilson Fellowship nominees will be interviewed this week in the second stage of their screening.
spans.names: The candidates are seniors Phoebe Babbage, East Aurora, N.Y.; Bruce Gensemer, Cleveland Heights O.; George Iden, Bloomingburg, O.; Peter Latimer, Cleveland Heights, O.; Jerry Sell, Delaware; Jack Van Horn, Pulaski, Pa.; Robert E. Zimmerman, Akron, O.; and Robert O. Zimmerman, Hiram, O.
spans.stipend: The students who survive the screening and following examinations will be in line for a $1,500 stipend to finance graduate work in humanities and social science.
spans.nationalPool: The 2,000 candidates who receive interviews represent approximately 25 per cent of the original nominees.

1980-01-31-5.headline: New Stuy Security Policy; ID's Checked After 11:30

spans.admissionRule: only Stuyvesant Hall residents be admitted to the building after 11:30 p.m. All others must be escorted by a Stuyvesant Hall resident.
spans.idCheck: Student security aides will check all student identification cards.
spans.dutyEnd: The security aide will be on duty until 7 a.m.
spans.unescortedVisitor: the new policy allows a non-escorted student to call the Stuyvesant resident he is visiting. He must come to the lobby and escort the non-resident to the room.

spans.result: The women's track team set three new school records and placed sixth, with 13 points, among Division I, II and III teams in the All-Ohio meet at Ohio State Saturday.
spans.relay880: The 880-yard relay team of sophomore Pebbles Muller, freshmen Amanda Osborn and Lynn Rhoden and senior Sabrina Spencer placed sixth and bettered the 1979 OWU record of 1:51.2 by one second.
spans.distanceMedley: The distance medley relay team of freshmen Liz Einfeldt, Nena Lenfest and Barb Sweeney and junior Margie Morris placed fifth with a time of 13:17.1, breaking last year's record of 13:18.
spans.twoMile: Einfeldt, Lenfest, Sweeney and sophomore Lisa Foster ran a 10:14 in the two-mile relay, breaking last year's record of 10:20.

spans.event: Benjamin Hooks, executive director of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP), will present "Where Do We Go From Here?" Tuesday at 8:15 p.m. in Gray Chapel.
spans.topic: In his lecture, Hooks will explore the historical development and current status of blacks in America.
spans.tickets: Tickets are $4 for the general public, $2 for students and can be reserved at the MUB desk.

spans.systemAge: the University's phone system was implemented 10 years ago, and since has fallen behind the times.
spans.study: the trustees approved a $50,000 study on the feasibility of renovating the system.
spans.target: the aim is for 1992 at the latest.
spans.businessImpact: It hurts our college business 50 percent

1988-01-20-3.headline: Faculty meeting centers on Austin Hall, parking problem

spans.closureAndPlan: Austin Hall closed in 1984. In the fall of 1986 plans were made to renovate the residence hall into Austin Manor, a living unit for students and retired alumni.
spans.approval: On appeal, however, the credit was approved and work has begun.
spans.openingEstimate: Warren estimated that the building would be ready for "an occupant" by next November or December.
spans.parking: Students aren't supposed to park in the faculty lots until after 5 p.m., but Judd said that cars are parked there as early as 3.

spans.headliner: On April 16th at 9p.m. the Blues Traveler will perform in Branch Rickey
spans.tickets: Tickets for the concert will go on sale one month before the show, March 16, and will cost $15. Branch Rickey has a seating capacity of 2,000
spans.opener: Ohio Wesleyan's very own Ugly Stick will open for Blues Traveler.
spans.schedule: Ugly Stick is scheduled to begin playing at 7:30p.m. and will be followed by Blues Traveler at 9 p.m.

bandPhoto.caption: Blues Traveler
bandPhoto.scanCaption: Blues Traveler are, from the right, Chan Kinchla, Bobby Sheehan, John Popper and Brendan Hill.

1997-01-22-17.headline: Early Childhood Center Offers Learning Opportunities

spans.ages: The children at the ECC range in age from three to five years
spans.familiesAndWorkers: the ECC serves 110 families, The Center employs professional teachers and 29 OWU students through the work-study and Student Assistantship (StAP) programs.
spans.learningModel: The children are encouraged to learn by exploring all of their senses

classroomPhoto.caption: an OWU student assists a child with a project at the Early Childhood Center

spans.consolidation: The Academic Resource Center (ARC), in the R. W. Corns Building, combines the Academic Skills Office, Writing Resource Center and Qualitative Skills Center in one location.
spans.facilities: The ARC also houses a library of writing reference materials, three computers and plenty of study space.
spans.director: Donna Dawson, a former high school math teacher, is the director of the new ARC.
spans.locationAndContact: The ARC is located on the third floor of the Corns Building. Students should call x3925 to schedule an appointment.
